title: LeggettPlus: A Guide to the Lead PBPK Simulator
text: LeggettPlus provides open-source, reproducible implementation Leggett+ physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model lead (Pb). model originally developed Richard Leggett (1993) later updated Vork, Carlisle Brown (2013); Vork & Carlisle (2020); Vork, Brown, Carlisle (2023). package includes: leggett_base_parameters() — build physiological parameter set run_leggett_model() — solve 21-compartment ODE system across one exposure stages summarize_leggett_output() — extract compartment values, maxima, AUC model run launch_leggett_app() — start bundled Shiny application

title: LeggettPlus: A Guide to the Lead PBPK Simulator
text: LeggettPlus intended research, regulatory evaluation, exposure-scenario exploration. Outputs interpreted within context model assumptions, parameter uncertainty, available toxicokinetic data. package intended clinical diagnosis individual medical decision-making. Male-reference physiology. package’s physiological parameters calibration constants (body weight, hematocrit, blood-volume scaling, RBC binding capacity) derived adult male / male-dominated occupational-worker data (Leggett, 1993, subsequent updates). female-specific parameter set implemented — separate hematocrit range, blood-volume expansion, RBC binding capacity female individuals, including pregnancy. Simulated results assumed represent female physiology.

title: LeggettPlus: A Guide to the Lead PBPK Simulator
text: ODE system tracks lead mass (µg) following compartments: Blood lead level (BLL, µg/dL) derived quantity computed rbc + plasd + plasb divided blood volume. state variable calculated summarization.

title: LeggettPlus: A Guide to the Lead PBPK Simulator
text: simulation requires stage schedule — data frame row represents discrete exposure period (stage). columns must present.
code: library(LeggettPlus)  # Single-stage example: background oral intake only, no inhalation schedule <- data.frame(   # ---- Time ----   duration = 365,               # Length of this stage in DAYS (integer; rounded if fractional)    # ---- Non-inhalation background intakes (µg/day) ----   # These represent all non-air occupational sources: ingestion of   # contaminated dust, dermal absorption, dietary lead at the worksite, etc.   Occ.background.ug.d = 0,      # Occupational background (µg/day) — set 0 if air is the only source    # Non-occupational background: diet, drinking water, consumer products, soil/dust   # ingestion at home. FDA interim reference level for adults is 8.8 µg/day from food.   NonOcc.background.ug.d = 2.2, # Non-occupational background (µg/day)    # ---- Airborne lead concentrations (µg/m³) ----   Occ.pb.ug.m3    = 0,          # Airborne Pb at the workplace (µg/m³);                                  # OSHA PEL = 50 µg/m³; OSHA action level = 30 µg/m³    NonOcc.pb.ug.m3 = 0.15,       # Ambient airborne Pb outside work (µg/m³);                                  # NAAQS rolling 3-month average = 0.15 µg/m³    # ---- Breathing rates (m³/DAY) ----   # The model uses daily rates. Convert hourly rates by multiplying by 24.   # OEHHA Air Toxics Hot Spots Guidance (2015) provides age/activity-specific   # rates in L/kg-day (residential) or L/kg-8h (worker) that must first be   # converted to m³/day using body weight.   Occ.breath.rate.m3.d    = 30, # Occupational (worker) daily breathing rate (m³/day)   NonOcc.breath.rate.m3.d = 17, # Non-occupational (residential) daily breathing rate (m³/day)    # ---- Work schedule ----   work.hour.perweek = 40,        # Hours worked per week; used to partition                                  # occupational vs. non-occupational exposure time.                                  # Set to 0 for scenarios without a workplace.    # ---- Oral intake (µg/day) ----   # Direct oral uptake entering the GI tract. Absorb fraction is controlled by   # abs_ratio in run_leggett_model() (default 0.20 for adults).   oral.intake.ug.d = 0           # Any additional direct oral dose not already in                                  # the background columns (e.g., a supplement or                                  # experimental bolus). Usually 0 for field scenarios. )  out <- run_leggett_model(schedule) head(out$time_series) #>   time       plasd        evf      rbc       plasb       csf       cex #> 1    0 0.000000000 0.00000000 0.000000 0.000000000 0.0000000 0.0000000 #> 2    1 0.003916887 0.01206443 1.594497 0.002658280 0.1634495 0.0440129 #> 3    2 0.004485538 0.01382104 3.331099 0.005555387 0.2579576 0.1497212 #> 4    3 0.004925894 0.01518127 5.067053 0.008453616 0.3164784 0.2901984 #> 5    4 0.005321016 0.01640202 6.766953 0.011293982 0.3587878 0.4524617 #> 6    5 0.005694420 0.01755597 8.421100 0.014060289 0.3939920 0.6306438 #>            cne       tsf        tex          tne     livhu        livlu #> 1 0.000000e+00 0.0000000 0.00000000 0.000000e+00 0.0000000 0.0000000000 #> 2 5.811589e-06 0.2047953 0.05514819 5.384159e-06 0.2745786 0.0009095225 #> 3 4.130440e-05 0.3232100 0.18760776 3.826752e-05 0.5914247 0.0038919058 #> 4 1.243008e-04 0.3965345 0.36364643 1.151647e-04 0.9261270 0.0091307390 #> 5 2.652577e-04 0.4495468 0.56700071 2.457680e-04 1.2713637 0.0167159128 #> 6 4.712132e-04 0.4936571 0.79032102 4.366029e-04 1.6239655 0.0267037203 #>       strpd      stmid       stslo       brain      kidoth        sint #> 1 0.0000000 0.00000000 0.000000000 0.000000000 0.000000000 0.000000000 #> 2 0.2780072 0.03534436 0.007090809 0.001063334 0.001417142 0.003047339 #> 3 0.3654524 0.07829441 0.015754631 0.002361940 0.003146468 0.003975670 #> 4 0.4127227 0.12599315 0.025427670 0.003811144 0.005074853 0.004843106 #> 5 0.4499684 0.17761368 0.035950112 0.005386896 0.007170061 0.005696806 #> 6 0.4838429 0.23281006 0.047257625 0.007079478 0.009418985 0.006548065 #>       kidurp       lintu       lintl #> 1 0.00000000 0.000000000 0.000000000 #> 2 0.03303783 0.007156867 0.005211387 #> 3 0.06904372 0.011117017 0.013140774 #> 4 0.10506338 0.014151665 0.019937136 #> 5 0.14036373 0.016971300 0.025811258 #> 6 0.17474347 0.019742737 0.031230006

title: LeggettPlus: A Guide to the Lead PBPK Simulator
text: leggett_base_parameters() computes static physiological values initial state vector. can inspect override defaults, note body_weight_kg hematocrit male-reference values: defaults , RBC binding saturation constant feed (Sat.ug.dL leggett_base_parameters()), calibrated adult male / occupational-worker data. female-specific hematocrit range blood-volume expansion implemented. Additional parameters passed run_leggett_model():
code: params <- leggett_base_parameters(   body_weight_kg    = 73,     # Body weight (kg). Scales blood volume and OEHHA breathing-rate conversions.                               # Reference value from adult male occupational-worker data.   hematocrit        = 0.3802, # Fractional hematocrit (0–1). Determines RBC vs. plasma volume split.                               # Default is the reference adult male value used in Leggett (1993);                               # no female-specific default is provided.   age_years         = 40,     # Age at start of simulation (years). Influences some kinetic parameters.   initial_bll_ug_dl = 0.78    # Initial blood lead level (µg/dL) before new exposures begin.                               # CDC NHANES 50th-percentile for US adults (2015–16) is 0.78 µg/dL. )  # Derived blood volumes (dL) params$blood_volume_dl #> [1] 54.2025 params$rbc_volume_dl #> [1] 20.60779 params$plasma_volume_dl #> [1] 33.59471

title: LeggettPlus: A Guide to the Lead PBPK Simulator
text: example occupational scenario provided : 20 years workplace exposure followed 20 years retirement background exposure .
code: schedule_occ_ret <- data.frame(   duration = c(     20 * 365,  # Working years (days)     20 * 365   # Retirement years (days)   ),   Occ.background.ug.d = c(25, 0),    # Occupational non-air background: 25 µg/day at work, 0 in retirement   NonOcc.background.ug.d = c(2.2, 2.2), # Non-occupational background stays constant   Occ.pb.ug.m3 = c(30, 0),           # Occupational airborne Pb: 30 µg/m³ during work, 0 in retirement   NonOcc.pb.ug.m3 = c(0.15, 0.15),   # Ambient Pb stays constant   Occ.breath.rate.m3.d = c(30, 0),   # Worker breathing rate during exposure; 0 when retired   NonOcc.breath.rate.m3.d = c(17, 17),   work.hour.perweek = c(40, 0),       # 40 h/week during work; 0 in retirement   oral.intake.ug.d = c(0, 0) )  out_ret <- run_leggett_model(   stage_schedule    = schedule_occ_ret,   body_weight_kg    = 73,   hematocrit        = 0.3802,   age_years         = 30,             # Age at simulation start (will be 30 when work begins)   initial_bll_ug_dl = 0.78 )  nrow(out_ret$time_series)  # total days simulated #> [1] 14599

title: LeggettPlus: A Guide to the Lead PBPK Simulator
text: pulse scenario models discrete, acute exposure events separated recovery intervals. pulse represented one-day stage elevated Occ.background.ug.d equal pulse dose.
code: # Background stage between pulses background_stage <- data.frame(   duration                = 29,   # days between pulses   Occ.background.ug.d     = 0,   NonOcc.background.ug.d  = 2.2,   Occ.pb.ug.m3            = 0,   NonOcc.pb.ug.m3         = 0.15,   Occ.breath.rate.m3.d    = 0,   NonOcc.breath.rate.m3.d = 17,   work.hour.perweek       = 0,   oral.intake.ug.d        = 0 )  # Pulse stage: same as background but with a one-day dose pulse_stage <- background_stage pulse_stage$duration <- 1 pulse_stage$Occ.background.ug.d <- 500  # µg delivered in one day  # 3 pulses each separated by 29 background days pulse_schedule <- do.call(rbind, replicate(3, rbind(pulse_stage, background_stage), simplify = FALSE))  out_pulse <- run_leggett_model(pulse_schedule)

OEHHA Air Toxics Hot Spots Guidance (2015) provides age- activity-specific rates can converted follows: Residential (non-occupational): Table 5.6 gives rates L/kg-day. Convert m³/day: Worker (occupational): Table 5.8 gives 8-hour rates L/kg-8h. Convert m³/day: Shiny app automates conversion OEHHA mode selected, using appropriate age band activity intensity Tables 5.6 5.8. Job presets map common occupational categories (e.g., Farming, Office Work) Table 5.8 intensity bands.

what: Worker Adjustment Factor and Discount Factor (WAF/DF)
title: LeggettPlus: A Guide to the Lead PBPK Simulator
text: lead source operates intermittently (e.g., 8 h/day, 5 days/week), annual average concentration -represents exposure. OEHHA Eq. 5.4.1.2 defines Worker Adjustment Factor (WAF): : H_source = hours per day source active D_source = days per week source active DF = Discount Factor (1.0 unless partial shift overlap applies) standard 8 h/day, 5 d/week scenario full overlap, WAF ≈ 4.2. app’s WAF/DF block Exposure Inputs panel computes automatically adjusts occupational air concentration accordingly.
code: WAF = (24 / H_source) × (7 / D_source) × DF

title: LeggettPlus: A Guide to the Lead PBPK Simulator
text: Three scenario templates available (app via schedule data frame directly): Occupational — Steady workplace non-occupational exposures fixed duration. Use single continuous exposure period planned change. Key inputs: airborne concentrations, breathing rates, background intakes, working hours per week. Occupational Retirement — Adds post-work stage occupational air background set zero (lower ambient level). Use project long-term BLL decline cessation assess whether bone mobilization keeps BLL elevated. Key decision: many retirement years simulate, whether retain ambient non-occupational exposure. Pulse — Models discrete, time-limited exposure events separated recovery intervals. Use sporadic high-dose situations (e.g., occasional welding, remediation activities, experimental bolus doses). Key decisions: pulse dose (µg), number pulses, inter-pulse interval (days). background stage pulses controls baseline load.

title: LeggettPlus: A Guide to the Lead PBPK Simulator

title: Physiologically Based Pharmacokinetic Model for Lead (Leggett+)
text: See vignette full documentation schedule columns, scenario types (occupational, retirement, pulse), breathing-rate conversions, output interpretation.
code: library(LeggettPlus)  # 1. Define exposure stages (one row per stage) schedule <- data.frame(   duration                = 365 * 20,  # days   Occ.background.ug.d     = 25,        # non-air occupational intake (µg/day)   NonOcc.background.ug.d  = 2.2,       # non-occupational background (µg/day)   Occ.pb.ug.m3            = 30,        # occupational airborne Pb (µg/m³)   NonOcc.pb.ug.m3         = 0.15,      # ambient airborne Pb (µg/m³)   Occ.breath.rate.m3.d    = 30,        # worker breathing rate (m³/day)   NonOcc.breath.rate.m3.d = 17,        # residential breathing rate (m³/day)   work.hour.perweek       = 40,        # hours worked per week   oral.intake.ug.d        = 0          # additional direct oral dose (µg/day) )  # 2. Run the model out <- run_leggett_model(schedule, age_years = 30, initial_bll_ug_dl = 0.78)  # 3. Summarize at a time point summarize_leggett_output(   out$time_series,   time_point       = 365 * 10,   blood_volume_dl  = out$metadata$blood_volume_dl,   plasma_volume_dl = out$metadata$plasma_volume_dl,   rbc_volume_dl    = out$metadata$rbc_volume_dl )  # 4. Or use the Shiny app launch_leggett_app()

title: LeggettPlus 0.2.0
text: CRAN preparation: added @return tag launch_leggett_app(), cleaned DESCRIPTION (author formatting, removed unresolved arxiv tag), added spelling wordlist Language field, expanded unit test coverage ~99%, added lint, test-coverage, pkgdown GitHub Actions workflows alongside existing R CMD check workflow. tab: introduced two-column layout pairing app overview, “Intended Use Limitations,” “Leggett+ Simulates” sections LeggettPlus logo, enlarged logo, added consistent spacing sections. tab: added “Source Code & R Package” section pointing power users GitHub codebase installing LeggettPlus R package directly (remotes::install_github()) scripted/programmatic use. Fixed stray indentation tab’s install-code snippet.

title: LeggettPlus 0.1.0
text: Initial CRAN submission. Removed NIOSH/OSHA (related MIOSHA/ACOEM/AOEC/CDPH/ABLES/CSTE) blood lead level interpretation classification features Shiny app, including guidance-band lookup table, “Interpretation (NIOSH/OSHA)” results panel, downloadable HRA note, corresponding -tab guidance section reference. app package now report simulated BLL values without applying occupational medical-surveillance thresholds. Renamed run_app() launch_leggett_app(). Expanded README vignette documentation (installation, key functions, compartment reference, worked examples).
